findings.severity: major (cross-artifact binding; not a defect of F0's own declared scope, but must be reconciled before any F0-bound schema passes)
findings.field: classes.AF-WCC-VAC-GEN.conclusion.text (lines 193-194) vs schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml statement_formal (lines 56-57, 244) and f0_binding.declared_f0_sha256 (line 304)
findings.finding: F0's declared WCC conclusion binds the pair '(s,delta)' ('For every admissible (s,delta) there is a comeager set G_{s,delta}'), while F1 at f0_binding 0abb9ed8 freezes statement_formal over a tagged index r in D0 where D0 is the disjoint union 'smooth | (sobolev,s,delta)'. A reader who binds the F0 anchor at this hash therefore gets a statement that does not range over the smooth branch the schema quantifies over. F0 itself defers the data class to F1 (H4 unresolved:true, genericity_value_status provisional_owned_by_F1), so this is a binding-form divergence, not a false class claim.
findings.falsifier: A frozen revision in which F0's WCC conclusion quantifies over the same index set as the schema's statement_formal (either F0 adopts r in D0 including the smooth branch, or F1 scopes statement_formal to the Sobolev branch), with the schema's f0_binding refreshed to that revision.

findings.field: field_vocabulary.genericity_topology (lines 142-147) and the four classes[].axes blocks
findings.finding: The vocabulary declares genericity_topology with allowed values {unresolved, named_by_F1, named_by_F2} and states that a generic-quantified claim 'must name genericity_kind AND genericity_topology'. All four class conclusions are generic-quantified, but NO class instance carries genericity_topology (the token occurs only at lines 144, 145 and in the T1 guard at 502). Consequently the T1 guard 'genericity_kind and genericity_topology must match exactly' is not evaluable at F0. The rule can be read as claim-level (the vocabulary section addresses downstream claim records) or class-level; the artifact does not disambiguate, so two careful readers disagree.
findings.falsifier: A revision in which each class's axes carry genericity_topology (e.g. named_by_F1/named_by_F2/unresolved), or in which the vocabulary rule and the T1 guard are explicitly scoped to claim records so the class-level omission is no longer a rule violation.

findings.severity: moderate (wording may assert more than the class's stated content; no formal inflation because the predicate that follows is correct)
findings.finding: The scalar-class conclusion asserts 'The singularities that form are hidden behind an event horizon', which asserts black-hole-region formation. The taxonomy elsewhere refuses to make that assertion part of WCC: candidate_consequences.C1 for AF-WCC-VAC-GEN explicitly quarantines 'the black-hole region B = M \ J-(I+) has non-empty interior' as unresolved and NOT part of the definition, and the companion lists 'black hole formation' among the WCC non_goals. The formal tail-negation predicate in the same conclusion is correct and the file claims no theorem, so this is a wording defect (asymmetry between the two WCC classes), not a promoted result.
findings.falsifier: A revision whose scalar conclusion states only the visibility/tail predicate (no event-horizon or black-hole-region assertion), or a recorded ruling that the event-horizon gloss is part of the class definition and that C1 is correspondingly promoted.

findings.severity: minor (guard pointer does not resolve to the named symbol)
findings.finding: G3 points downstream linters at 'artifacts/worker-01/validate_taxonomy.py (MERGED_REGULARITY_RE + normalization)', but that file defines MERGED_RE (line 34) and normalize_regularity (line 37); the symbol MERGED_REGULARITY_RE lives in artifacts/worker-01/a1_metrics_probe.py (line 56). A downstream linter following the pointer verbatim finds no such symbol, which is exactly the re-derivation the guard forbids.
findings.falsifier: A revision whose G3 pointer names a symbol that resolves in the cited file (or cites a1_metrics_probe.py:56 for MERGED_REGULARITY_RE).

findings.severity: minor (registration surface split between declared taxonomy and registry)
findings.finding: The companion binds the H2_loc negative test case to 'variant H2LOC of AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN'. H2LOC is registered in artifacts/formulation/VARIANT_REGISTRY.json (parent_class AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN, status registered_variant_not_written) and in the supplement's implication_ledger, but the declared taxonomy's variants block registers only SET and CH. A reader of the canonical F0 artifact alone cannot resolve H2LOC.
findings.falsifier: A revision listing H2LOC in the canonical variants block with parent_class AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN, or a companion rewrite that no longer implies F0-level registration of H2LOC.

findings.severity: minor (metalinguistic cross-reference inside a frozen conclusion field)
findings.finding: The scalar conclusion embeds a revision note calling its superseded wording 'the variant SET predicate', but variant SET is registered with parent_class AF-WCC-VAC-GEN, a different class. The note is metalinguistic and explicitly says the old reading is NOT this class's predicate, but a reader scanning the frozen conclusion could misread the scalar class as owning variant SET.
findings.falsifier: A revision that moves the rev5 annotation out of conclusion.text into revision metadata, or that registers the scalar reading under its own parent_class + variant_id.

findings.severity: note (supplement-only resolution; explicitly not a contradiction)
findings.field: canonical classes.AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN.hypotheses.H4 (lines 340-342) vs companion axis_registry.extension_equation_requirement (lines 150-153) and C0 contract (lines 89-93)
findings.finding: The canonical C0 class leaves the metric-versus-embedding regularity subtlety unresolved (machine_checkable false, unresolved true, owned F2/L1); the supplement freezes the C0 extension class as bare continuous metric with no equation requirement and forbids substituting the distributional-Ricci variant.
